categories.claimBoundary: Compares observable CommonJS results for the reviewed public and runtime-package imports; it does not cover every helper export or bundler resolver.

categories.requirement: disable, no-memo, pure, and diagnostic suppression
categories.claimBoundary: Compares the reviewed directive and suppression outcomes, including the pure mutation barrier; it is not an exhaustive optimizer equivalence claim.

categories.requirement: JSX event and delegation behavior plus DOM mutation

markers: Rust compiler output preserves Core reactive runtime behavior
captured reactive aliases remain mutable after an event

categories.claimBoundary: Input, form submission, keyboard, focus/blur, callback-ref cleanup, and portal behavior are compared across compiler outputs in JSDOM with one shared current runtime. This proves compiler-output alignment for the reviewed scenario, not every legacy DOM fixture or legacy-runtime equivalence.

categories.requirement: anonymous, member, and wrapped component roles

markers: anonymous, indirect, assigned, wrapped, registry, or object-member functions

categories.claimBoundary: These 24 Babel-accepted roles are explicit Rust rejections with a migration contract, not cross-implementation runtime parity.

markers: configured reactive scopes accept member, optional member, and global hosts

categories.claimBoundary: Compares one member-host callback result across compilers and separately checks native member, optional-member, and global host recognition.

markers: compile and analyze consume the same resolved metadata snapshot

categories.claimBoundary: Compares seven reviewed Babel and Rust CommonJS graphs across hook return shapes, reactive exports, barrels, namespaces, wrapper chains, type-only edges, and reserved export names. It also exercises the versioned Rust host snapshot and real Vite graph convergence, but does not claim equivalence for every isolated legacy import fixture.

categories.requirement: CommonJS, ESM, and physical, graph, and public identity combinations

markers: request matrix covers every source identity and structured request dimension

categories.claimBoundary: Compares legacy-compatible request dimensions structurally and labels Rust-only public and graph identity fields as native host protocol rather than Babel equivalence.

categories.requirement: async, generator, class, decorator, and TypeScript option matrix

markers: standard decorators fail closed before emitting unsupported syntax

categories.claimBoundary: Compares reviewed async, generator, class-field, namespace, and enum results; raw standard decorators are an explicit fail-closed diagnostic contract, not runtime parity.

categories.requirement: SSR output, hydration claims, and Preview resume behavior

markers: Rust matches Babel 0.28 SSR and hydration semantics

categories.claimBoundary: Compares static renderToString structure, strict DOM-node claiming with eager updates, and snapshot-driven resumable clicks across compiler outputs using one shared current SSR/runtime pair. It does not claim legacy-runtime ABI, streaming, Suspense, or exhaustive SSR equivalence.

categories.requirement: per-position source maps through complex lowering
categories.claimBoundary: Checks exact authored line and UTF-16 column mappings for reviewed native lowerings plus legacy-compatible input-map composition; it does not assert identical Babel and Rust generated-token layouts.

categories.requirement: runtime results for all 22 reviewed capability expansions

markers: runtime probes cover every reviewed Rust capability expansion exactly once

categories.claimBoundary: Executes each Rust capability expansion exactly once and binds it to its reviewed corpus row; Babel rejected these inputs, so this is deliberately not cross-implementation runtime parity.
